ci.yml.rig:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'rig')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all tier (the nightly), ubuntu and windows in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap), ubuntu alone in a pull
        # request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_rig || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # 75 was the measured windows number with the native lane DARK there
    # (46:46 over two lanes). sc43 lights the third lane on that host and
    # the budget said the number could not be assumed for three.
    # MEASURED over the two runs of `ec5087e`: windows **48 min** (from
    # 46:46 — the third lane costs about ninety seconds, because most of
    # what it meets here it declines by name), macOS 31 min. 90 leaves
    # headroom over the windows number without pretending 75 was
    # re-earned on a host that now runs half again as many invocations.
    #
    # sc81: WINDOWS OUTGREW 90, so its leg alone gets 120; ubuntu and
    # macOS keep 90 (not re-measured here). The windows rig's job time on
    # trunk's runs: 45.4, 50.5 min at `b1babae` and `3111d39` (11-03,
    # 11-05); then the public-PKI rows landed (`d4a4d4c`: x/crypto/rsa and
    # x/crypto/p384 each about 11 min there, x/tls/cert 3 more, nearly all
    # of it lupin's step budget on rows it declines, about 37 s a row) and
    # the same commit ran 89.5, 68.6 and 89.3 min (11-05, 11-06, 11-07);
    # `2411d86` (scrypt and passwd, 4.3 min more) 85.6 min green on 11-10
    # and cut at 90 on 11-08 and 11-09. The same rows ran 1.30 times
    # slower on one runner than another (68.6 against 89.5), and the
    # slowest whole job seen is 89.5 min; 120 is 1.34 times it.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.os == 'windows-latest' && 120 || 90 }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        # No `submodules:` — upstream/ is private and CI cannot clone it
        # (deploy keys disabled org-side); sync-pin runs snapshot-only.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: fmt
        run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - name: clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: test (rig internals; binary-guarded tests SKIP loudly)
        run: cargo test --workspace
      - name: sync-pin
        run: cargo xtask sync-pin
      # sc42 / wolf-std#16 — THE OBSERVATION LANES, RELIT.
      #
      # Every earlier revision of this step was an `echo SKIP`, because
      # neither upstream published a release archive keyed to the pins.
      # Both do now (wolf v0.2.9, four archives; lupin v0.1.30, five
      # assets), so the runner gets the same two binaries the author's
      # box has, and `std-test`, `gen-vectors --check`, `doc-examples`
      # and `ulp` stop doing their static half only.
      #
      # The model is wolf-lang's own sibling-pairing step (its
      # `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), and the two rules it earned are kept
      # verbatim:
      #   * NEITHER THE VERSION NOR THE DIGEST IS TYPED IN. The versions
      #     come out of `vendor/tools.toml`, which is the file `doctor`
      #     gates against, so this step tracks the pin instead of
      #     repeating it and the next bump costs zero edits here. The
      #     digest is read off the release asset GitHub reports and
      #     checked against the bytes that arrived (ws21).
      #   * A PIN NAMING A RELEASE THAT DOES NOT EXIST REDS BY NAME.
      #     Absence stopped being the normal state at this pin; a missing
      #     asset is now a bug in the bump, not a lane that is dark, and
      #     the loud SKIP that used to stand here would hide it.
      - name: acquire the pinned wolf and lupin, by digest, from their releases
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The two live `version =` keys of vendor/tools.toml, in file
          # order: [lupin] first, [wolf] second. Superseded values in that
          # file are commented out, so `^version` matches exactly two lines.
          lver=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' vendor/tools.toml | head -1)
          wver=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' vendor/tools.toml | tail -1)
          test -n "$lver" && test -n "$wver" || { echo "::error::vendor/tools.toml names no version"; exit 1; }
          # The runner's triple, by name. An unknown host reds here rather
          # than guessing an asset that would 404 three lines later.
          case "$RUNNER_OS-$RUNNER_ARCH" in
            Linux-X64)     triple=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu;  lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            Linux-ARM64)   triple=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            macOS-ARM64)   triple=aarch64-apple-darwin;      lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            Windows-X64)   triple=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc;    lz=zip;    exe=.exe ;;
            *) echo "::error::no release triple for $RUNNER_OS-$RUNNER_ARCH"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          # lupin's windows asset is a ZIP and wolf's is a tarball —
          # measured, not assumed, and the one asymmetry in the ten files.
          wa="wolf-$wver-$triple.tar.gz"
          la="lupin-$lver-$triple.$lz"
          sha256() {
            if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
            else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
          }
          fetch() {  # repo tag asset -> dl/asset, verified against the reported digest
            local repo="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3"
            local want
            want=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets \
                     --jq ".assets[]|select(.name==\"$asset\")|.digest")
            test -n "$want" || { echo "::error::$repo $tag publishes no $asset"; exit 1; }
            gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --pattern "$asset" --dir dl
            local got; got=$(sha256 "dl/$asset")
            test "$got" = "${want#sha256:}" || {
              echo "::error::$asset digest mismatch: reported ${want#sha256:}, arrived $got"; exit 1; }
            echo "$asset  sha256 $got  OK"
          }
          rm -rf dl .wolf-bin && mkdir -p dl .wolf-bin
          fetch wolffe-lang/wolf-lang   "v$wver" "$wa"
          fetch wolffe-lang/wolf-interp "v$lver" "$la"
          # Both archives carry one top-level directory. wolf's holds the
          # driver, the cimport worker and the native rung's runtime
          # archive side by side, which is exactly the layout
          # `xtask/src/bins.rs` resolves (`.wolf-bin/`, then
          # `native_rt()` looking beside the driver), so it lands whole.
          tar -xzf "dl/$wa" -C .wolf-bin --strip-components=1
          # sc58: since wolf 0.2.27 the archive carries `std/` (wolf-std at
          # `std/STD-REV`) and the compiler reads it when nothing names a
          # root. The rig stages THIS checkout's `std/` and passes
          # `--std-root` on every invocation, so the bundled copy is never
          # the subject here; it is removed so that no invocation can fall
          # back to it and pass on a std this commit did not write.
          if [ -d .wolf-bin/std ]; then
            echo "archive std at $(cat .wolf-bin/std/STD-REV 2>/dev/null || echo '(no STD-REV)'): removed, the rig stages this checkout's std/"
            rm -rf .wolf-bin/std
          fi
          case "$lz" in
            tar.gz) tar -xzf "dl/$la" -C dl ;;
            # git-bash on the windows image does not ship `unzip`
            # everywhere; python3 does, on all three images, and its
            # zipfile is the same on each. Try the tool, keep the
            # guarantee.
            zip)    if command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then unzip -q "dl/$la" -d dl
                    else python3 -c "import sys,zipfile;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "dl/$la" dl
                    fi ;;
          esac
          cp "dl/lupin-$lver-$triple/lupin$exe" .wolf-bin/
          chmod +x ".wolf-bin/wolf$exe" ".wolf-bin/lupin$exe" || true
          # Say what arrived. A lane that goes dark later must not be able
          # to blame acquisition without this log contradicting it.
          ls -l .wolf-bin
          ".wolf-bin/wolf$exe" --version
          ".wolf-bin/lupin$exe" --version
      - name: doctor
        run: cargo xtask doctor
      - name: ledger-check
        run: cargo xtask ledger-check
      # sc44 — **std-test RUNS ON ALL THREE HOSTS AGAIN, and the thing
      # that was killing ubuntu is fixed upstream rather than worked
      # around here.** wolf-std#19 and the timing half of wolf-std#20
      # were ONE BUG seen through two ceilings, which is what sc43 said
      # in writing; wolf-lang#308 is the fix and v0.2.11 carries it.
      #
      # `[exec.checked.budget]` (s153, spec/05 §5) gives the checked tier
      # a BYTE budget beside its step budget — 256 MiB, charged at every
      # allocation, never refunded — so the tier answers `unsupported`
      # instead of growing. The clause's own prose names this
      # repository's row: "one wolf-std row reached 16.6 GiB of resident
      # set on a 16 GB runner before `step budget exhausted` arrived — an
      # OOM where an honest refusal was owed."
      #
      # Re-measured at sc44 on the author's box, the three rows that did
      # it, cold, `/usr/bin/time -l`, checked tier:
      #
      #   cavp_sha256_long   30.2 MiB   1.57 s   unsupported
      #   cavp_sha384_long   40.4 MiB   1.82 s   unsupported
      #   cavp_sha512_long   40.0 MiB   1.79 s   unsupported
      #
      # Against F-0116's 16-18 GiB and 6.7 s, that is a factor of four
      # hundred in bytes and four in time. Predicted 45-55 MiB before
      # measuring and it came in UNDER the band. The most expensive
      # single process left in the whole differential is lupin's own
      # refusal of the same rows at 0.63 GiB.
      #
      # So both ceilings come off together:
      #   * ubuntu runs the differential again — the shutdown signal was
      #     the tier's allocation and the tier is bounded now;
      #   * the 60 s per-row ceiling stands UNCHANGED and no longer
      #     binds, because the rows that blew it finish in under two
      #     seconds. `STD_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` is still not set: sc43's
      #     answer to wolf-std#20's either/or was NEITHER, and it is
      #     still neither. Nothing here was relaxed.
      #
      # sc47 / wolf-std#34 — UBUNTU GOES REQUIRED, AND THE ADVISORY HOST
      # STOPS BEING SILENT.
      #
      # The marker above was `${{ runner.os != 'macOS' }}` for four
      # sprints, and it hid a RED windows differential through two
      # lanes' readings of it (wolf-std#20 stated a windows green twice
      # on that reading and was wrong both times). The mechanism is
      # worse than "the job says success": at run 34672768728 the REST
      # API reports `conclusion: success` for this step on
      # `rig (windows-latest)` as well — a `continue-on-error` step's
      # conclusion is rewritten at BOTH levels, so "read the step
      # conclusion, not the job's" is not enough on its own. The only
      # two things that still carry the truth are the step's own log
      # (`xtask: RED`, `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1`)
      # and `steps.<id>.outcome`, which is the PRE-rewrite result.
      #
      # Two changes, and neither of them relaxes anything:
      #
      # 1. UBUNTU IS REQUIRED. `std-test: GREEN` on `rig (ubuntu-latest)`
      #    at four consecutive heads — 34602166418 (527fa44),
      #    34618995826 (7582e7a), 34668184512 (d116bcb) and
      #    34672768728 (8b5a18e). sc44 made it advisory for "the first
      #    completion at the new budget"; that completion has now
      #    happened four times and the reason has expired. The marker
      #    narrows from `!= 'macOS'` to `== 'Windows'`.
      #
      # 2. WINDOWS STAYS ADVISORY AND SAYS SO OUT LOUD. Three native
      #    net/process rows are red there (wolf-std#34) and they are a
      #    std.net/std.process question, not this lane's. But the
      #    verdict step below reads `outcome` beside `conclusion` and
      #    prints both, so the divergence between them is ONE GREPPABLE
      #    LINE in every future run instead of a hunt through 400 rows,
      #    and an advisory RED raises a `::warning::` annotation that
      #    `gh run view` surfaces.
      #
      # The marker stays spelled `continue-on-error` rather than moving
      # into the script, deliberately: `xtask/src/workflow.rs` now reads
      # this key and `selftest.rs` gates it against a blessed list that
      # carries the issue number, so an advisory step cannot be added,
      # widened, or left behind its issue without the `rig` job going
      # red on every host. Hiding the advisory-ness inside a shell
      # variable would have put it back where no checker can see it.
      #
      # `run:` stays a bare `cargo xtask std-test` on its own line
      # because `workflow::cargo_invocations` matches the invocation
      # verbatim; a `; rc=$?` tail would make this step read LOCAL-ONLY.
      - name: std-test (the differential; three lanes, three hosts)
        id: std_test
        # REQUIRED on all three hosts since 14f0ab2 (wolf-std#34), which
        # retired the windows advisory marker once the 180 s ceiling below
        # had held six runs. The history that follows is why it existed.
        # THE REASON CHANGED AT sc51, and the old one is retired:
        # wolf-std#34's three native net/process rows were fixed at sc48,
        # and the three json STACK OVERFLOWS that replaced them are GONE
        # -- s161 gave the checked machine its own 64 MiB stack, wolf
        # 0.2.15 ships it, and two full windows runs at this pin
        # (35223247575, 35265207587) contain no `1073741571`, no
        # STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW and no "overflowed its stack" anywhere.
        # Those rows answer ledger words now.
        #
        # What keeps windows advisory is NEW and smaller: the lupin lane
        # flakily blows std-test's 60s wall-clock ceiling on the long
        # crypto vectors, and the set MOVES between runs -- three rows at
        # 35223247575 (p256/rfc6979_p256, p256/sign_verify_smoke,
        # sha2/cavp_sha384_long), a different two at 35265207587
        # (sha2/cavp_sha384_long, sha2/cavp_sha512_long). ubuntu and
        # macOS time out on none of them. That is a runner-speed ceiling,
        # not a wrong answer, and the fix is to raise
        # STD_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS on windows and prove it over consecutive
        # runs -- which is its own change, not a rider on a pin bump.
        #
        # sc52 RAISES THAT CEILING, ON WINDOWS ALONE, TO 180 s. The five
        # rows are not slow answers. They are step-budget refusals:
        # `cavp_sha{256,384,512}_long`, `p256/rfc6979_p256` and
        # `p256/sign_verify_smoke` are `unsupported` on lupin because
        # lupin runs to its 50M-evaluation-step budget and then refuses.
        # The step count is the same on every host, and the time taken to
        # reach it is the runner's speed. `windows-latest` runners differ
        # by about 1.8x from run to run: this step took 1574 s to 2801 s
        # over the nineteen windows logs sc52 read. On the slow runners
        # the five rows land at 55-70 s, per-test, from the log's own
        # timestamps (F-0139). Every other host keeps 60 s. std-test now
        # ends with its slowest invocations against the ceiling, so the
        # margin is printed on every run and not inferred from a green.
        # The marker stayed until that table had held on consecutive runs;
        # it held six, and 14f0ab2 dropped it.
        #
        # `workflow::ADVISORY_STEPS` is empty since 14f0ab2: a
        # `continue-on-error` added here without blessing it there reds
        # `rig` on all three hosts.
        env:
          STD_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '180' || '60' }}
        run: cargo xtask std-test
      # No step in this file is advisory since 14f0ab2 (the step above was
      # the last). This one stays so that an advisory step, if one is ever
      # blessed again, is never quiet:
      # `outcome` is what the step DID, `conclusion` is what
      # `continue-on-error` rewrote it to, and printing the pair is the
      # cheapest possible version of the rule wolf-std#34 had to learn
      # by being wrong twice.
      - name: std-test verdict (outcome vs conclusion, wolf-std#34)
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          outcome='${{ steps.std_test.outcome }}'
          conclusion='${{ steps.std_test.conclusion }}'
          echo "std-test verdict on $RUNNER_OS: outcome=$outcome conclusion=$conclusion"
          echo "- \`std-test\` on **$RUNNER_OS**: outcome \`$outcome\`, conclusion \`$conclusion\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if [ "$outcome" = failure ] && [ "$conclusion" = success ]; then
            echo "::warning title=std-test is RED on $RUNNER_OS and ADVISORY::cargo xtask std-test exited non-zero; continue-on-error rewrote the conclusion of the step AND of the job to success. This host gates nothing for std-test. See wolf-std#34."
            echo "std-test verdict: ADVISORY RED on $RUNNER_OS — this host gates nothing for std-test (wolf-std#34)"
          fi

  # sc41 / F-0113 / wolf-std#13 — the lane nothing lit, now lit and REQUIRED.
  #
  # `cargo xtask ci` runs eleven steps; the `rig` job above runs seven of
  # them. The four below — lint-conventions, gen-vectors --check,
  # doc-examples and ulp — had never executed on a runner in this
  # repository's history, which is why a broken `net.write` doc example
  # (F-0112) was green on all three platforms for four sprints: no runner
  # had ever executed a `wolf-doc-example`. They run here, in the
  # gauntlet's own order, one job per host.
  #
  # Deliberately NOT `needs: rig`. `ci()` is fail-fast, so locally these
  # four really do come after the seven; but a job that is skipped when the
  # seven are red teaches nothing on the run where it is most needed, and
  # the whole point of this lane was to be read. Ordering is preserved
  # WITHIN the job; the two jobs are independent across it.
  #
  # BUDGET vs MEASURED (docs/findings.md, "The sc41 CI lane"). The budget
  # was written before the first run; the measurement is the second run,
  # green on all three hosts, and it was wrong by more than an order of
  # magnitude in the cheap direction:
  #
  #   ubuntu   budget  6 min   measured 20 s
  #   macOS    budget  7 min   measured 37 s
  #   windows  budget 20 min   measured 50 s
  #
  # `timeout-minutes: 20`, down from the first landing's 45 and matching
  # `rig`, with the headroom deliberate rather than slack: every
  # observation lane is DARK here (no release artifacts at the pins), so
  # doc-examples currently stages 421 examples and executes none of them.
  # The day the binaries publish, this job starts running 421 programs on
  # three lanes and these numbers stop applying.
  #
  # `continue-on-error` was GONE at sc41 (cc30524), after two green runs
  # on all three hosts, and the one red the lane produced was F-0114 —
  # the rig's own, not any runner's.
  #
  # It is GONE AGAIN at sc42, on every step of THIS job, after two green
  # runs on three hosts at `4a98793` — the `push` run 34518522469 and the
  # `pull_request` run 34518526783 of the same commit, six green jobs
  # each, with the logs read line by line rather than the conclusions
  # trusted. That last clause is not decoration: a `continue-on-error`
  # step that exits 1 still reports `conclusion: success`, which is how
  # sc42 briefly recorded a RED windows differential as green.
  #
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # sc42 — AND THEN THE LANES CAME ON, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT JOB.
  #
  # sc41's numbers stop applying exactly as its own comment predicted
  # they would: "the day the binaries publish, this job starts running
  # 421 programs on three lanes". That day is this commit. The four
  # steps below are ADVISORY again for one landing, and so are `rig`'s
  # `doctor` and `std-test`, for the reason sc41 gave when it did the
  # same thing: a step that has never executed on two of three tier-1
  # runners cannot be made required by a branch that cannot verify them,
  # and the first run is to be READ, not to be passed.
  #
  # BUDGET, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST LIT RUN, constant term first:
  #
  #   CONSTANT TERM (acquisition) — two `gh release view` calls, two
  #   downloads, two digest checks, two extractions. Bytes per host:
  #   ubuntu 68.9 MB + 2.4 MB, macOS 13.7 MB + 2.1 MB, windows 11.7 MB
  #   + 2.0 MB. MEASURED on the author's box by running this step's own
  #   script (macOS, over a home link, both `gh release view` calls
  #   included, a loaded box): **8.0 s**. Budget on a runner, whose link
  #   to GitHub's own release storage is not a home link: **60 s on
  #   every host**, ubuntu highest because its wolf archive is five
  #   times the others.
  #
  #   ONE THING IS PREDICTED RED BEFORE THE RUN, so that reading the run
  #   is a check and not a story: the windows archive ships the native
  #   rung's runtime as `wolf_rt.lib`, and `bins::native_rt()` looks for
  #   `libwolf_rt.a` (or `$WOLF_RT_LIB`). So the windows NATIVE lane is
  #   expected to print its loud SKIP with the file sitting right beside
  #   the driver — dark for a reason that is a FILENAME, which is the
  #   F-0114 shape one function over. Left unfixed for this landing on
  #   purpose: it is a prediction until the log says it.
  #
  #   VARIABLE TERM (execution) — the local gauntlet is the reference,
  #   since it is now the same gauntlet. Measured step by step on the
  #   author's box (macOS aarch64, a LOADED box carrying a sibling
  #   lane's gauntlet, binaries at the pins, `.lu` counts as of this
  #   commit): lint-conventions 0 s, gen-vectors --check 1 s, doc-examples
  #   **164 s** (421 blocks x 3 lanes), ulp 0 s — and, in the other job,
  #   std-test **911 s** (397 tests x up to 3 lanes). The differential is
  #   5.5x the doc examples and is the term that matters; `gates`, the
  #   job sc41 built and budgeted, is the CHEAP one now.
  #
  #   BUDGET on the runners, setup and cold xtask build included:
  #     ubuntu   `rig` 30 min, `gates` 10 min
  #     macOS    `rig` 30 min, `gates` 10 min
  #     windows  `rig` 75 min, `gates` 25 min
  #   The windows multiplier is 2.5x, not sc41's guessed 10x, because
  #   sc41's own measurement retired the 10x guess (5.5x on a staging
  #   workload, and the constant term dominated everything). What is
  #   NEW and unbudgetable from here is process spawning: ~1,700
  #   compiler and interpreter invocations per host, and the native rung
  #   links a binary for each of its share of them.
  #
  # See docs/findings.md, "The sc42 relit lane", for this budget's
  # reasoning and for what the first lit run actually cost.
  #
  # `timeout-minutes` went UP to 90 for the first landing, from the 20
  # that was right for a job staging 421 examples and executing none of
  # them. MEASURED over three lit runs, it comes back to **20 for
  # `gates`** and **75 for `rig`**:
  #
  #   job     host     budget    measured (run 1 / run 2)
  #   gates   ubuntu   10 min    2:35 / 2:44
  #   gates   macOS    10 min    3:30 / 3:31
  #   gates   windows  25 min    2:48 / 2:46
  #   rig     ubuntu   30 min    29:02 (runner killed) / 0:33 (skip, #19)
  #   rig     macOS    30 min    29:51 / 29:37
  #   rig     windows  75 min    45:32 / 46:46
  #
  # `gates` came in at a QUARTER of its budget on every host and `rig`
  # came in at the budget exactly on macOS and at 62% on windows, which
  # is the split the variable-term note predicted: doc examples are
  # cheap and the differential is not.
  # sc43: `gates` came in at a quarter of its budget on every host with
  # the windows native lane dark. wolf-std#18 lights it, so `doc-examples`
  # stages 421 blocks against THREE lanes on that host instead of two and
  # the third one links a binary per block. The landing budgeted 60
  # minutes for that; MEASURED over the two runs of `ec5087e`, windows
  # came in at **3 minutes** and so did ubuntu and macOS. Back to 20,
  # which is where the measurement puts it.
ci.yml.gates:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'gates')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all and full tiers (on macOS the merge's smoke,
        # tl30), ubuntu alone in a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_gates || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      # sc42 / wolf-std#16 — THE OBSERVATION LANES, RELIT.
      #
      # Every earlier revision of this step was an `echo SKIP`, because
      # neither upstream published a release archive keyed to the pins.
      # Both do now (wolf v0.2.9, four archives; lupin v0.1.30, five
      # assets), so the runner gets the same two binaries the author's
      # box has, and `std-test`, `gen-vectors --check`, `doc-examples`
      # and `ulp` stop doing their static half only.
      #
      # The model is wolf-lang's own sibling-pairing step (its
      # `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), and the two rules it earned are kept
      # verbatim:
      #   * NEITHER THE VERSION NOR THE DIGEST IS TYPED IN. The versions
      #     come out of `vendor/tools.toml`, which is the file `doctor`
      #     gates against, so this step tracks the pin instead of
      #     repeating it and the next bump costs zero edits here. The
      #     digest is read off the release asset GitHub reports and
      #     checked against the bytes that arrived (ws21).
      #   * A PIN NAMING A RELEASE THAT DOES NOT EXIST REDS BY NAME.
      #     Absence stopped being the normal state at this pin; a missing
      #     asset is now a bug in the bump, not a lane that is dark, and
      #     the loud SKIP that used to stand here would hide it.
      - name: acquire the pinned wolf and lupin, by digest, from their releases
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The two live `version =` keys of vendor/tools.toml, in file
          # order: [lupin] first, [wolf] second. Superseded values in that
          # file are commented out, so `^version` matches exactly two lines.
          lver=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' vendor/tools.toml | head -1)
          wver=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' vendor/tools.toml | tail -1)
          test -n "$lver" && test -n "$wver" || { echo "::error::vendor/tools.toml names no version"; exit 1; }
          # The runner's triple, by name. An unknown host reds here rather
          # than guessing an asset that would 404 three lines later.
          case "$RUNNER_OS-$RUNNER_ARCH" in
            Linux-X64)     triple=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu;  lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            Linux-ARM64)   triple=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            macOS-ARM64)   triple=aarch64-apple-darwin;      lz=tar.gz; exe= ;;
            Windows-X64)   triple=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc;    lz=zip;    exe=.exe ;;
            *) echo "::error::no release triple for $RUNNER_OS-$RUNNER_ARCH"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          # lupin's windows asset is a ZIP and wolf's is a tarball —
          # measured, not assumed, and the one asymmetry in the ten files.
          wa="wolf-$wver-$triple.tar.gz"
          la="lupin-$lver-$triple.$lz"
          sha256() {
            if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
            else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
          }
          fetch() {  # repo tag asset -> dl/asset, verified against the reported digest
            local repo="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3"
            local want
            want=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets \
                     --jq ".assets[]|select(.name==\"$asset\")|.digest")
            test -n "$want" || { echo "::error::$repo $tag publishes no $asset"; exit 1; }
            gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --pattern "$asset" --dir dl
            local got; got=$(sha256 "dl/$asset")
            test "$got" = "${want#sha256:}" || {
              echo "::error::$asset digest mismatch: reported ${want#sha256:}, arrived $got"; exit 1; }
            echo "$asset  sha256 $got  OK"
          }
          rm -rf dl .wolf-bin && mkdir -p dl .wolf-bin
          fetch wolffe-lang/wolf-lang   "v$wver" "$wa"
          fetch wolffe-lang/wolf-interp "v$lver" "$la"
          # Both archives carry one top-level directory. wolf's holds the
          # driver, the cimport worker and the native rung's runtime
          # archive side by side, which is exactly the layout
          # `xtask/src/bins.rs` resolves (`.wolf-bin/`, then
          # `native_rt()` looking beside the driver), so it lands whole.
          tar -xzf "dl/$wa" -C .wolf-bin --strip-components=1
          # sc58: since wolf 0.2.27 the archive carries `std/` (wolf-std at
          # `std/STD-REV`) and the compiler reads it when nothing names a
          # root. The rig stages THIS checkout's `std/` and passes
          # `--std-root` on every invocation, so the bundled copy is never
          # the subject here; it is removed so that no invocation can fall
          # back to it and pass on a std this commit did not write.
          if [ -d .wolf-bin/std ]; then
            echo "archive std at $(cat .wolf-bin/std/STD-REV 2>/dev/null || echo '(no STD-REV)'): removed, the rig stages this checkout's std/"
            rm -rf .wolf-bin/std
          fi
          case "$lz" in
            tar.gz) tar -xzf "dl/$la" -C dl ;;
            # git-bash on the windows image does not ship `unzip`
            # everywhere; python3 does, on all three images, and its
            # zipfile is the same on each. Try the tool, keep the
            # guarantee.
            zip)    if command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then unzip -q "dl/$la" -d dl
                    else python3 -c "import sys,zipfile;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "dl/$la" dl
                    fi ;;
          esac
          cp "dl/lupin-$lver-$triple/lupin$exe" .wolf-bin/
          chmod +x ".wolf-bin/wolf$exe" ".wolf-bin/lupin$exe" || true
          # Say what arrived. A lane that goes dark later must not be able
          # to blame acquisition without this log contradicting it.
          ls -l .wolf-bin
          ".wolf-bin/wolf$exe" --version
          ".wolf-bin/lupin$exe" --version
      - name: lint-conventions
        run: cargo xtask std-test --lint-conventions
      # sc45 / F-0117 / wolf-std#21 — THE GATE D34 NEVER HAD.
      #
      # `fmt` in the `rig` job gates the RUST (`cargo fmt --all --check`)
      # and has since sc00. Nothing in either job gated the WOLF, so
      # "`wolf fmt` is law for every committed `.lu` here" was a sentence
      # in commit messages and in `vendor/tools.toml` with no mechanism
      # behind it — and thirty-two committed files were off the fixed
      # point at wolf 0.2.9, 0.2.10 AND 0.2.11, the three sorted lists
      # equal line for line. Standing drift, never a bump artefact,
      # invisible because nothing looked (F-0113's shape one gate over).
      #
      # It runs in `gates` rather than `rig` because it needs the wolf
      # binary this job has already acquired, and beside
      # `lint-conventions` because it is the other static reading of the
      # same `.lu` files. MEASURED on the author's box over 452 files at
      # 0.2.11: **0.23 s** for the whole tree in one process; the step
      # batches at 64 paths per invocation (windows caps a command line
      # at 32,767 characters and this list only grows), so budget seven
      # invocations and call it two seconds on any host.
      #
      # REQUIRED from the first run, and that is deliberate against this
      # repository's own custom of one advisory landing: the advisory
      # rule is for a step whose BEHAVIOUR on a host is unknown. This
      # step's behaviour is known on every host — it is one process
      # comparing bytes, it was run to completion here before the push,
      # and the tree it reads is committed. A `continue-on-error` on it
      # would reproduce exactly the thing being fixed.
      - name: fmt-lu
        run: cargo xtask fmt-lu
      - name: gen-vectors --check
        run: cargo xtask gen-vectors --check
      # These two were ADVISORY ON WINDOWS for one commit — the landing
      # that lit the native lane there (wolf-std#18) — and the advisory
      # marker is GONE AGAIN, on the same evidence sc42 required: two
      # greens, read LINE BY LINE rather than off the job's colour,
      # because a `continue-on-error` step that exits 1 still reports
      # `conclusion: success`.
      #
      # The two runs of `ec5087e`, `gates (windows-latest)` in each:
      #   doc-examples: 421 block(s), GREEN   (370 of them on the NEW
      #     native lane, every one `exit(0)` — which is also the proof
      #     that the rung LINKS on that host, the question sc42 left
      #     untested)
      #   ulp: native reproduces all 200 recorded values exactly; GREEN
      #
      # And the budget written before the run was wrong by an order of
      # magnitude in the cheap direction, which is worth the two lines
      # it costs to say: `gates (windows-latest)` was budgeted at 60
      # minutes for 421 examples gaining a linking lane and came in at
      # **3 minutes**, because most of what the native rung meets in
      # this tree it declines by name rather than compiles.
      - name: time-oracle (10,000 cells against host date; BSD on macOS, GNU on Linux)
        run: cargo xtask time-oracle
      - name: doc-examples
        run: cargo xtask doc-examples
      - name: ulp
        run: cargo xtask ulp
      # sc84, wolf-std#151: no integer division in the objects generated
      # for curve25519, chacha20/Poly1305, sha2 and bech32 (default and
      # release, the runner's own target), and their release builds still
      # answer the published vectors. Windows SKIPs it loudly (COFF, no
      # disassembler acquired); ubuntu and macOS carry it.
      - name: codegen (no division in the crypto modules' objects; release vector rows)
        run: cargo xtask codegen

  # The run's verdict, and its name: `tier full`, `tier pr` or `tier noop`.
  # It needs every job, runs unless the run was cancelled, and fails unless
  # the plan succeeded, the jobs and hosts it chose are the tier's, every
  # chosen job succeeded and every other job was skipped (ci/tiers.py
  # verdict). lane-audit.sh reads this job's name and conclusion.
ci.yml.tier:
name: tier ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs:
      - plan
      - rig
      - gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: every chosen job succeeded, every other was skipped
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict

  # A red nightly opens an issue (ruling #92): a scheduled run has no lane
  # watching it, so the red has to come and find one. One open issue per
  # workflow, its title the dedupe key; a further red night comments on it
  # (ci/nightly-red.sh, tested by ci/tiers-test.py T8). Never on a pull
  # request, a push or a dispatch: those reds have a lane attached already.
ci.yml.nightly-red:
name: nightly red, an issue
    needs: tier
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: open or update the nightly-red issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: ci/nightly-red.sh

nightly.yml.drift:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: acquire LATEST implementation binaries
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same pre-M1 honesty as ci.yml: no release artifacts exist
          # yet, and the upstreams are private to this token. When they
          # publish, fetch the latest here (NOT the pin) so std-test
          # reports drift between recorded pins and reality.
          echo "SKIP: no upstream release artifacts published — drift lane dark"
      - name: doctor (report drift, never gate)
        run: cargo xtask doctor
      - name: std-test against latest
        run: cargo xtask std-test
